title.label: Does one thing and does it well!

content.label: Interface is clean and responsive, the app doesn’t feel sluggish at all. Records your data smoothly and then shows it to you how you want it, exactly how a habit tracker should. Developer is active and responsive to feedback. Pro subscription offers a lifetime option which is greatly appreciated in a sea of apps and services where you keep paying up every month for no additional value and could lose features if you don’t go up a tier at any time.
The best habit tracker I've found. Beautiful, fluid, and doesn’t get in the way. The developer is responsive and helpful. Really impressed.

Been using HabitKit daily for 2 years now and it’s become my go-to habit tracker. Clean interface, no bloat, just works. The widget support is excellent for quick check-ins.

One small wish: a basic read-only API would open up automation possibilities for power users, but that’s a nice-to-have.

Highly recommended for anyone serious about building habits.

It is clean, simple, and actually makes habit tracking enjoyable. No clutter nor overcomplication. I use it daily and it’s easily one of my favorites.

Highly recommend

It’s a good app! I have the pro version and as much as I enjoy it, I do not feel that the pro version should cost as much as it does. The app does not have enough features to justify the $13 pro. $5 or $10 would be more acceptable. Also, there is a fixed amount of colors that you can make your habits that you’re tracking, and of the 21 available colors, 4 of them are just different shades of grey. I really wish there was access to a color wheel or something so you can select more colors. The blues and greens that are available are way too similar. I, and I’m sure many others, need a lot of visual variety when tracking habits like this. And when you’re tracking over 10 habits, it gets difficult to visually distinguish between 4 shades of grey and 6 shades of mildly different blueish green

title.label: Great habit tracker!  Worth the price

content.label:
I spontaneously bought the lifetime access because I want to start tracking certain daily and weekly things I wanted to do or not do.  I have been using for 2 months now every day.  It’s great! 

It’s customizable, yet not confusing.  As a UX/UI designer myself, I appreciate the balance of simplicity and flexibility. 

Only improvements I’d love to see are the ability to have an anti-streak calculator for habits I’m trying to break, and some more robust reporting in terms of trends.

Overall a great, daily app!  Get it!

Awesome app, better than Atoms and all the other habit trackers. The price to unlock all features ($2/month, $12/year) is reasonable and affordable. I upgraded to the yearly subscription after trying it out for a week. This is fun to use which means I’ll keep using it. I like that you can add a corresponding emoji to each habit and include a habit description. I also like that you can set streak goals in multiple ways. This app just has all the best features. I’m thankful it exists.

I’ve tried a number of habit tracking apps, but this one just works for me. It’s been fun and flexible to customize, and I find myself checking it daily. Better yet I added my habits as a stacked widget on one of my iPhone home screens and it’s been satisfying to swipe through and check off set habits each day. I had a small feature request, sent feedback to the developer and same day, he mentioned this feature was already on the roadmap. Was impressed with the response time. Glad to support this independent developer and his great app which has improved my life!
I am really enjoying this app.  It is simple to use and reasonably priced.  I reached out to the developer with a possible recommendation and he emailed me back immediately.  Highly recommend!

title.label: No bad habit tracking and No Apple Watch support.

content.label: I’m dissatisfied with the app. I purchased only to find out that it does not include bad habit tracking, only requires you to use work around. The app also does not have an Apple Watch app. Please integrate these and I will update my review.

Really great app but lacks cloud syncing which seems crazy for an app entering 2026 and is the main reason I am hesitant to pay for the premium subscription. I also don’t understand how the app counts streaks for “x times per week” habits. I’m on a 12 week streak for a habit I started 8 weeks ago.

This app checks a few boxes for me:
It allows me to see the trends of my habits over time; allowing me to see what i need to improve or fix. 
I can easily keep track of habits in multiple areas of my life, from working out, studying, and down to simple things like remembering to water my plants. 

While I can use notes, or a to-do list, or alarms, HabitKit allows you to come to one place for all of that-in a more fun and satisfying place. 

Honestly, the colors, icons, calendar, and organization through putting habits in certain categories keeps everything neat and aesthetically pleasingly. Everyone has their way of doing what this app does, but the way habit kit does it is what allows me to use it this thoroughly. Actually, it makes keeping in touch with my goals and to-dos fun-something lacking from other apps whether pre-installed, or otherwise. 

Being able to see your goals and habits stack up or lack over time is the big indicator on how well/poor Im doing, and thats the motivator for however you choose to track your trends. 

Long time user of the app, and I’ll keep on using it to perfect my routine. Well done Habitkit, looking forward to future updates that reflect the simple brilliance you have here already.

I know the app isn't abandoned, but it feels abandoned. No cloud sync or cloudkit. No Mac app. No bad habit mode that automatically checks off days. No custom icon support (icon library very limited). No custom colors. It just feels abandoned. With a couple weekends of work the developer could be making double what they are making now with a few tweaks. C'mon!

title.label: Great, simple, intuitive, bug-free as far as I can tell. Nice app.

content.label: Great, simple, intuitive, bug-free as far as I can tell. Nice app.

I recently turned started using a minimalist phone setup to help me to be more productive. A key part of the design was adding HabitKit widgets to my home screen. It's very motivating to see your habit history packed into a beautiful little chart, with the ability to check off (or increment) habits without having to open the app. After making these changes to my phone, this past week has been the most productive week of my life, and I sincerely believe HabitKit has been the main reason for that. 

The support is also incredible. I reached out to the solo developer via email, asking him about 2 different features I was hoping he could add to the app. 2 days later, he got back to me, in a very friendly and well-thought-out email. In this email, he told me that he had already been working on adding the first feature, and the other had been added to his todo list. Given that he is a solo developer, and also working on another up-and-coming app at the same time, I'd say his support services are the best I've ever seen, from any app on the app store.

Seriously loving this app so far - it’s pretty much exactly what I was looking for. Thank you for offering a one-time purchase option - it’s rare these days and you’re awesome for that

Two suggestions:

> negative habits
- basically the opposite of a regular habit, allowing you to set a limit for how many times a day, if any before the color turns off
- this could even be as simple as a habit that auto-completes at the start of the day, but you can go back and manually uncheck it

> web app
- it’s a big ask, but even just like a dashboard accessible on the web would be fantastic

keep up the good work
I bought the lifetime subscription, but the widget is not unlocking. Great app but would like this feature to be fixed. Thank you!
Awesome App and I can’t wait till we have iCloud compatibility
This is a wonderfully designed app. Simple, intuitive, adaptable. Everything you need, nothing you don’t.

HabitKit is by far the best habit tracker I have used… and I have used several. It is sleek and simple, yet customizable. 

The options for viewing my habits are perfect for the ways in which I think about them- in both the short and long term. I can manage my day-to-day easily with a high-level, consolidated view of all my habits, while still being able to see the big picture over an extended period of time with a GitHub-esque chart. 

Bonus points for a responsive developer, and continued improvements. Highly recommend.

I wanted to use it so I would read my Bible daily and this was the only app that helped, highly recommend. 
P.S. Keep it free

I’ve been looking for a good Habit tracking app on iOS. I tested seven and ended up choosing this one. I really like the simplicity, aesthetic, straightforwardness, and overall good usability of this app. Also the pro version is also of the cheapest out there. $2 a month, or $30 lifetime. Compared to $10 a month and $90 lifetime pro versions. I recommend it!

HabitKit is hands-down the best habit app I’ve used. It has enabled me to set up old hotel key cards as NFC triggers — when I tap one for my morning supplements, it marks the habit complete, reads the weather, starts my playlist, and tells me my calendar for the day. Everything just flows. The design is clean, automations work flawlessly, and the developer is super responsive. Absolutely worth it!

I’ve been using it for a month and haven’t seen any bugs. I love the visual style more than any other habit app, and it’s the main reason I chose it. HabitKit just feels good to use, and that’s important for an app you use daily.
I really like this app, it reminds me of GitHub but I wish the widgets allowed me to see more then one habit at a time, or gave me a overview.

I’ve been using this app for almost two months now to track the days I drink enough water. The layout itself is pretty self explanatory and simple, and the lack of ads makes it very easy to log on and check off a streak without distractions and wasting time. The free version of Habitkit works very well if you have a few habits you want to track, and works perfect despite not being premium. I personally hate when developers force users into buying a subscription for the basic features their app has been made to offer by nagging with constant ads and an overall worse experience with the app, so Habitkit is one of the rare gems among many slop apps who suffer from such issues.

Thank you, developer!
La app se ajusta a lo que uno busca perfectamente, visualmente es muy bonito y moderno, llevo meses usándolo y estoy muy contento, felicitaciones a los creadores
Can the icloud synchronous backup function be added?
I tried a handful of different habit trackers before landing on this one and I am really enjoying it so far!

HabitKit has been able to accomplish something that no other habit tracker has: I actually use it. The layout is so useful and logical, with all of the distracting junk stripped away. Its simplicity does not make it any less powerful, however. In fact, I think that is the thing that propels HabitKit ahead of all the others in terms of excellence. It strikes the perfect balance of simple and functional/customizable while also being beautiful. 

Data is powerful, but only if you can actually collect it. Now, I can.
I love seeing the grids as a way to visualize consistency! I have the paid version of the app, can't speak to the limits of the free version. Solid app.

title.label: The habit tracker I was looking for

content.label: Simple, effective, intuitive. Looks nice. Finally an habit tracker app I love!
This app is fantastic. Super simply and clear to use, it helping me a lot with practicing positive habits. I greatly appreciate the lifetime purchase option.
Very good habit tracker that has robust features as long as you pay for the pro version to unlock widgets.
After trying many apps, this is the one that just works. Other apps may work in a technical sense; however, this one sticks to the fundamentals, allowing use without thinking too much.

title.label: One of the best habit tracking apps - but NEEDS iOS Reminders integration and maybe APIs exposed ?

content.label:
This is by far the most visually appealing app. I was actually going to develop my own app which was similar to this, where it had the altair heatmap chart. But this goes beyond my initial idea and also has step counts/tiered counting. Moreover, the ease of completing a task with a tap, setting of reminders, color coding and the availability to switch between three different views is exactly what I needed.

This is way better than todoist, it is simple and intuitive. Most other apps have a lot of clutter and have too many details and clunky interfaces.

One important feature that is missing though is its integration with Calendar and Reminders. Not just that, PLEASE expose APIs to interact with the data, this would have a limited use case, but still could be very useful. For example, one could ingest their daily step count and automatically mark a habit. Another example is that say if I want to block a particular app unless I do X, it could allow it to do so. Lets say that I have a habit like “no scrolling videos in the morning for 2 hours”, I should be able to enforce this and mark the habit only when certain conditions outside the app are met - I know this is a little outside the scope of this app and probably would fit into another “habit enforcer” app that could integrate with this, but in any case this requires REST APIs to be exposed. I would love to partner with the dev and work on this idea.

This app is the exact thing I needed. It is simple and provides a visualization of goals. I can even quickly show the extent to which I reached a goal per day. Try it! It might be just what you’re looking for.

title.label: The best habit tracker I’ve used

content.label: I’ve tried a bunch of habit tracker apps, and honestly, they all felt like they were missing something until I came across HabitKit. It’s exactly what I needed. Great functionality, amazing design and actually helps me stay on track without feeling overwhelming. I’ve been using it every day, and it’s really helping me build better habits and move toward the kind of future I want. Super grateful I found this one. And I'm so happy that from today I'm subscribed to the pro version of HabitKit. :)

I purposefully chose a habit tracker a little down on the App Store because I wanted something simple,  it a lot of gadgets. This is it. Basic, won’t waste your time but will help you get your goals done.
I enjoy the interface and the functionality.
This app doesn't have notifications. So there's no way to get notified when to log a habit. I don't understand how this isn't a feature.

HabitKit is an awesome app if you like tracking your progress on anything. The UI is excellent and continues to receive quality updates, and the widgets are super convenient. The summary analytics are also a really nice touch. Easily worth the purchase price.
One of the few apps that I have ever paid for that I didn’t regret.

Way too much going on for something as simple as tracking “habits” the app is eye appealing, but anyone who wants to use it should not go through so much trouble trying to understand it. I still haven’t figured it out and I will be deleting after this review.
A well designed, simple, intuitive, and customizable habit tracking app. Highly recommend.
The value for money you get with this app is huge! It has been a growth catalyst for me in prioritizing and creating new habits. Get it - you won’t regret it!

Why no widgets? I downloaded this app because I wanted to make a habit for coding and track my progress even on the home screen. My favorite part about apps are the widgets, and I don’t know why you have to pay just to use widgets. I really like this app, but isn’t the no widgets without subscription thing a bit overkill?

This app is exactly what I was looking for: a way to visually understand my habits over time where I'm doing well, where I need to pick it up. It's extremely simple and simple to use. Not only that but the developer is extremely responsive. I sent him an email about something that I wanted, and he responded the next day. 5/5. Download this app if you're looking for any type of habit tracker.
Clearly shows my progress toward my nutrition goal.

I was skeptical at first on whether this app would be what I was looking for in a habit app. Some try to do too much and some are too watered down. This hits the right chord with me. Great UI. Especially a home view with a month’s worth of performance in one easy glance.
